llm.summary: This skill openly creates local research-paper alert subscriptions, queries OpenAlex, and registers OpenClaw cron jobs for scheduled summaries.

dimensions.detail: Use of OpenAlex, local JSON state, and OpenClaw cron is proportionate, while the curl fallback and cron subprocess calls should remain limited to the documented commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a markdown skill file and one Python helper script; I found no install hook, dependency fetch, or hidden startup action.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents the needed workflow and says to confirm scheduling changes, but it does not declare a separate narrow tool-permission manifest.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Cron jobs and data/subscriptions.json persist by design for daily alerts; this is disclosed and scoped to named paper_push subscriptions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The network queries, local subscription file, relevance scoring, and scheduled runs all fit the stated research-paper alert purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you want a local scheduled workflow: it will write subscription state under data/, query OpenAlex with your research topics, and create or remove named OpenClaw cron jobs when you add, update, or remove subscriptions. Do not put tokens or private channel credentials in the skill folder.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The artifact does request shell, network, local file, and cron capabilities, but those capabilities are described in the skill and align with scheduled paper alerts.
[E1] expected: OpenAlex transmission is disclosed and necessary for paper lookup; the inspected code sends search parameters and an optional mailto contact, not local secrets or stored recipient IDs.
[AST4] expected: The subprocess calls use argument lists with shell disabled by default; curl is a documented HTTPS fallback and openclaw cron is the disclosed scheduling mechanism.
[SDI-2] expected: Calling openclaw cron is broader than pure paper search, but it is central to the advertised subscription workflow and not hidden.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese output is hard-coded and repeatedly disclosed; this is a localization/usability limitation rather than evidence of deception or unsafe behavior.
